shared_elements: T-shaped monolithic pillar with broad head and narrower shaft
shallow low-relief carving on pale limestone
quadruped animal shown in profile on the shaft
horizontal band/register of repeated pattern across the pillar
allover geometric net/mesh or hatched patterning
excavation context with dry-stone rubble walling behind
justification: Both are the same class of object — a T-headed monolith bearing shallow, flat-relief carving in which a profile quadruped sits on the shaft below a horizontal patterned band, and both are photographed in situ against rough rubble walling, so the immediate impression is closely comparable. The difference is density and program: B carries a stacked, multi-register composition (arcades, zigzag band, several animals and birds) rendered with crisp modelling, while A's pillar is largely covered by a single loose net-like lattice with one faint animal and a plain rectangular recess, giving a far sparser and more eroded effect.
